Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase! The umpires have made their way out in the middle. Scotland Under-19 are seen in a huddle, near the ropes. Stephan Pascal and Adrian Weir will open up for the West Indies Under-19. Ruaridh McIntyre comes to bowl. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 206 is the target and West Indies Under-19 will be hoping for their batters to chase this. For Scotland Under-19, the onus is on their bowlers to provide early breakthroughs in the game and put the Windies under pressure. Which side will come out on top? Let's find out. Chase coming up shortly...

West Indies Under-19 will be pleased with their performance with the ball. They will certainly be on the happier side walking into the break. The West Indies Under-19 opening bowlers were putting pressure on the Scottish openers but weren't able to dismiss any one of them. The bowlers weren't expensive either, but they were a bit unlucky too, as there was plenty of play and a miss, but they could not find a single edge or play someone down in the powerplay or after that. But after 20 overs, all thanks to Nathan Edward, as he is the one who takes the first blood for his team. It was really important for the Windes as they were losing their temper and bowled and provided a lot of extras to Scotland Under-19. After that event, they didn't allow any big partnerships from their opposition and were picking up wickets on regular occasions. Till the end of the innings, Isai Thorne managed to get four wickets into his account. Nathan Edward Sealy picked up two, whereas Nathan Edward and Raneico Smith chipped in for one each. It is a challenging target for the Windies, but they have to make sure they won't lose wickets in the early stages of the inning.

Scotland Under-19 had a slow and pretty decent start, better than the first game against England. There weren't many boundaries to count on, but they were really good at running between the wickets with total communication. Their openers were living a narrow life from the start, as it was clear that the swings of the Windies were creating huge problems for them. But they survived the whole of it and were able to set up a partnership of 89 runs in 132 deliveries, which ended on the 22nd over. Alec Price tried to fill up the shoe for his team, blowing some boundaries, and Jamie Dunk, on the other hand, after receiving some lifelines, scored an important half-century, but he couldn't enjoy it much as he got dismissed just after a couple of overs. He ends up scoring 57 runs off 87 deliveries. Alec Price continued partnering with his skipper but had to walk down the hut on the 38th over. The lower middle-order batters did enough to cross the 200 mark and offer a suitable target to defend on.

Match number 13 of the ICC Under-19 World Cup sees a clash between West Indies Under-19 and Scotland Under-19 at the JB Marks Oval in Potchefstroom. Both teams come into the contest on the back of a loss against a couple of strong sides and that makes this game all the more crucial. West Indies Under-19 featured in the tournament opener against hosts South Africa in what was a fairly close game but they lost by 31 runs. We did see a few good performances with the ball but they really did struggle with the bat and had it not been for the enigmatic Jewel Andrew, West Indies Under-19 would have lost by a huge margin. The wicket-keeping batter struck a massive century and kept his team in the game but wickets kept tumbling down. It was only Nathan Sealy who took 3 wickets in the first innings who supported Jewel for a bit and made a fighting 33. Scotland Under-19 on the other hand were comprehensively beaten by neighbors England in their first game and will now find it really difficult to get out of this tough group. Batting first, Scotland Under-19 lost a couple of quick wickets before skipper Owen Gould and Jamie Dunk put on a steady stand. Nobody could play a big innings and the middle order didn't have any runs in it either as they were bowled out for 174 runs. With the ball as well they couldn't make any inroads in the early stages and conceded a 100-plus opening stand which killed the game. They did pick three wickets later on but those were mere consolation. Both teams need to improve majorly with the bat but overall as well and a win could prove to be vital in their chances of making it through to the next stage of the competition. Who are you backing?
